execute: Identify the narrow claim, observer, verified positive and negative membership, and raw responses. Random names are only negative candidates: wildcard accounts, provisioning and normalization can invalidate absence. Ensure both inputs have valid format and follow the same protocol. Compare semantic signals with recorded order, session, source, cooldown, counters and deployment; retain volatile raw values and declare exclusions. Timing requires bounded sampling with order control and a stated noise question. If requests fail before lookup, restore the normal control before interpreting equality. Retain transport errors rather than treating timeouts as rejection.
review: Support only a controlled signal tied to verified membership. A valid negative reproducing the positive signal refutes that signal's specificity, not all possible oracles. Invalid sessions, missing raw data, shared counters or unresolved noise leave the claim inconclusive. Stop invalid-observer repeats; reopen for changed membership, observer, counter policy, deployment or a new discriminating signal.
